newsitem.title: USA: CME cattle futures end mostly up, nearbys down.
newsitem.headline: CME cattle futures end mostly up, nearbys down.

text.p: Long liquidation and bear spreading combined to weighed on nearby CME live and feeder cattle futures while short covering and the spread action supported deferred months, traders said.
Concern that boxed beef values may be near a top, especially with the Thanksgiving Day holiday drawing nearer, weighed on December live cattle futures.

Retailer interest will turn to more traditional holiday items and the high price of choice beef could further avert retailer buying. The number of days between Thanksgiving and Christmas is also less this year, traders said.
Tight choice cattle supplies and the recent rise in beef values lent support early before futures retreated.

Lighter-weight choice beef prices at noon were quoted higher at $120.91 per cwt, the highest level since June 17, 1993. Bear spreading added to the loss but also lent support to back months despite expectations choice cattle supplies will rise going into next year, they said.

Cattle placements increased this fall as feed costs eased, which will lead to more cattle marketings by early 1997. Early expectations on Friday's USDA Cattle-on-Feed report pointed to larger on-feed supplies as of Nov 1 than the previous month.

Placements were seen up again over last year in October and on-feed supplies likely rose to near year-ago levels after being smaller earlier in the year. Analysts' estimates for November on-feed supplies were running between 97.6 and 100.5 percent of a year ago while October placement estimates ranged from 101.2 to 110 percent and October marketings, 95 to 100 percent.

Spreading accounted for part of the mixed prices. R.J. O'Brien bought February and sold December while Refco bought June and August and sold April and also bought June and sold February. Earlier spreaders bought April and sold February. RBH bought April and sold February and October late.
Pit sources also cited scatterd selling of December 68 calls and 67 puts options. Volatility in December was down about one percent, and February volatility was steady to weak.

Feeder cattle generally followed the lead of deferred live cattle contracts with lower corn futures adding to gains. A decline in the latest CME feeder cattle index weighed on spot November in thin dealings, traders said.
Live cattle closed 0.325 cent a lb lower to 0.050 higher with only December off at 67.750 cents. Feeder cattle were off 0.125 to up 0.200 cent with only January off at 64.600 cents.
